blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 1 ka bhai hai: akela inverse function \(\sin^{-1}x\), jis ka integral yaad nahi lekin derivative \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\) aata hai.
Chaal wohi: \(\sin^{-1}x \cdot 1\), first \(\sin^{-1}x\) aur second 1.
Parts ke baad \(\int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\) bachega; numerator mein \(x\) hai jo \(1 - x^2\) ke derivative \(-2x\) ka hissa hai, to yeh seedha nikal aata hai.
Plan: parts, phir chhoti si substitution, aur domain \(-1 < x < 1\) yaad rakhein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \sin^{-1}x\,dx\), \(-1 < x < 1\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: parts: \(f(x) = \sin^{-1}x\), \(g(x) = 1\).

Parts lagayein
\[= x\sin^{-1}x - \int x\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\), 1 ka integral \(x\).

Bacha hua integral
\[\int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx = -\dfrac{1}{2}\int (1 - x^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}}(-2x)\,dx\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{(1 - x^2)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\frac{1}{2}} = -\sqrt{1 - x^2}\]
Kyun: \(1 - x^2\) ka derivative \(-2x\) hai, is liye \(-\frac{1}{2}\) bahar rakh kar \(-2x\) andar banaya; phir power rule \(\int [f]^n f'\,dx = \frac{[f]^{n+1}}{n+1}\) with \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\).

Jor dein
\[= x\sin^{-1}x - (-\sqrt{1 - x^2}) + c\]
\[= x\sin^{-1}x + \sqrt{1 - x^2} + c\]
Kyun: formula ka minus aur integral ka minus mil kar plus.
Dhyan dein: yahan aakhri sign plus hai; bohat se bachche \(-\sqrt{1 - x^2}\) likh dete hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = \sin^{-1}x + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} - \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
\[= \sin^{-1}x\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{1 - x^2}\) ka derivative \(\frac{-x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\); fractions cancel aur \(\sin^{-1}x\) bacha.
